summary: Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned a master's degree from the University of Madras, studying under C. S. Sundaram. Supervised by Munni K. Agrawal, he completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University. He was affiliated with Salesian College in 2008.

Toni Huber works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Jim Wilson and completed his PhD at the University of Canterbury in 1993 under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He was a professor at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976), taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011), and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

Torakazu Doi (1902–1971) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926). Later, he held positions at Dokkyo University (~1964–1968) and Sagami Women's University (~1965–1971).

Torkel Brekke is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo (~1990–1995) and a doctorate at the University of Oxford (1996–1999) under Richard Gombrich. His posts include University of Oslo (~2001–2017), PRIO (2016–2020), Oslo Metropolitan University (2019–2023), and MF Norwegian School of Theology (2023).

Toru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992). He served as an associate professor at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) specialized in Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. After studying at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he spent his career at Kyoto University (1909–1945), serving as professor, dean, and director, and later headed the Institute of Eastern Culture (~1947–1955).
Toru Kumoi works in Buddhist studies. He has held positions at the Institute for Humanities Informatics and as a chief researcher at the Japan Institute of Digital Humanities (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara (1921–2000) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1941–1944). He later held academic posts at Ibaraki University (~1954–1967), the University of Tokyo (~1967–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After graduating from the University of Tokyo (1898–1902), he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Dongguk University (1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, where he was also an assistant (~1996–2000). He later held chief researcher posts at the Japan Institute of Digital Humanities (attested 2015) and the Institute for Humanities Informatics (attested 2016–2018).
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University (~1966–1975) and later held an academic post there (~1985–2017).

Toshifumi Goto is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg in 1982, having studied under scholars including Karl Hoffmann and Johanna Narten. He held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003–2012).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. A Keio University graduate, he held a chair there (1954–1981) and later worked at McGill University (1961, 1969–1975) and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963) and later lectured there. He served as an associate professor at Tokai Gakuin University (~1978–1988) and professor emeritus at International Buddhist University (~1988–2011).

Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and held an academic appointment, including as associate professor, at Nagoya University from around 1988 to 2019.

Toshiichi Endo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and a doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (1995), supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake. He served as a professor at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held affiliations with the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2015–2019), and was a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1981) and later held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1991–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2019), where he was a professor and project leader.

Toshinori Ochiai is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Kacho Junior College (attested 2001) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2004–2019), and as director of the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (attested 2020).
